newsitem.title: USA: Warming weather causes flooding in South Dakota.
newsitem.headline: Warming weather causes flooding in South Dakota.

text.p: Warmer weather caused flooding in parts of South Dakota Wednesday as runoff from melting snow spilled from rivers into low-lying areas.
But so far the state has been spared widsepread flooding from record amounts of snow that fell during the past winter along the North Dakota-South Dakota border.
"We've been lucky so far," said Jim Sawyer, spokesman for Gov. William Janklow.

Parts of six state or U.S. highways were closed to some or all vehicles and some farms and homes in rural areas were swamped. The problem areas are generally along the James, Vermillion and Big Sioux rivers in the eastern half of the state.
The long-range outlook for flooding was uncertain and will depend on temperatures and possible rainfall in the coming days, officials said.
